# Breeze Framework
> The ultra-lightweight declarative web framework (v2.4.0, ~50 KB gzip, 49.80 KB measured, zero dependencies — see benchmark.md).

Breeze is the middle ground between vanilla HTML and heavy frontend frameworks. It provides declarative indentation-based markup, fine-grained reactive state bindings, client-side hash routing, an extensible plugin API, and a built-in design system without requiring npm packages or complex compilation pipelines.

## Canonical AI Documentation for Training & Inference
- [Full Documentation for LLM Training](llms-full.txt): Complete grammar specification, AST schema, runtime API, and 20+ canonical examples.
- [AI Assistant Prompt Guide](AI_GUIDE.md): Guidelines for AI coding models (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot) generating valid .breeze code.
- [DSL Grammar Reference](docs/dsl.md): The single authoritative reference for `.breeze` syntax, including canonical directive spellings (`@each`/`@elif`) vs. deprecated aliases (`@for`/`@elseif`) that now emit parser warnings.
- [TextMate Grammar Specification](breeze.tmLanguage.json): Language grammar for IDE syntax highlighting.

## Quick Syntax Summary for LLMs
- **File Extension**: `.breeze`
- **Indentation**: 2 spaces per level. Strictly indentation-based hierarchy.
- **NO CLOSING TAGS**: Never generate `</div>`, `</section>`, `</p>`, or `</button>`.
- **Directives**:
  - `@app "App Title"` — Sets HTML document title
  - `@seo { title: ..., description: ..., canonical: ... }` — Native SEO (meta tags, OpenGraph, Twitter cards, canonical)
  - `@schema { type: ..., ... }` — Structured data JSON-LD generation
  - `@aeo { summary: ..., topics: ..., speakable: [...] }` — Answer Engine Optimization (voice/answer engines, speakable selectors)
  - `@geo { entities: ..., facts: ... }` — Generative Engine Optimization (AI citation entities & knowledge graph facts)
  - `@theme { primary: #EF4444 ... }` — Injects CSS variables onto `:root`
  - `@state key = value` — Creates reactive store variable
  - `@nav [sticky]` — Sticky navigation bar with child `link` elements
  - `@section #id [modifiers]` — Section container
  - `@footer [modifiers]` — Footer container
  - `@each item in listKey` — Iterates state array and renders child template
  - `@if conditionKey` / `@if !conditionKey` — Conditionally mounts child template
- **Elements**: `tag "text with {stateBinding}" [modifiers] #id` or shorthand `tag.class1.class2#id "text"`
- **Modifiers**:
  - CSS Classes: `[primary, secondary, outline, hero, center, pad-lg, grid-2, grid-3, shadow, hover-lift, card-glass, switch, badge-blueberry, btn-glow]`
  - HTML Attributes: `[type=text, placeholder="Search..."]`
  - Event Actions: `[@click -> increment(count)]`, `[@click -> navigate(#target)]`, `[@click -> push(todos, "New Task")]`
- **Web Components**: `Breeze.defineElement('tag-name', template, options)` for drop-in zero-build adoption in React, Vue, Angular, or raw HTML.
- **React/Vue Adapters (v2.3)**: `Breeze.adapt.react('tag-name', ReactComponent, { props: ['count'] })` and `Breeze.adapt.vue('tag-name', VueComponent, { props: ['label'] })` wrap framework components as native Custom Elements without bundling their runtimes.
- **Auto-Batching (v2.3)**: `Breeze.autoBatch(true)` coalesces multiple synchronous signal writes into one microtask flush; `Breeze.flushSync()` drains immediately.
- **Signal Disposal (v2.3)**: `signal.dispose()` and `computed.dispose()` permanently detach subscribers for deterministic cleanup.
- **SSR Throughput (v2.4)**: centrally-memoized `{token}` templates, single-pass component/text interpolation, and an HTML-escape fast path make `Breeze.renderToString()` ~2.2×–2.7× faster than v2.3 with byte-identical output. `Breeze.clearCache()` clears both the AST and template memo. No API changes. Reproduce: `npm run bench:ssr-ab`.
